hero: The quietest week is the one where you already know the numbers.
sub: Hoping takes energy. Knowing takes a morning. What you earned, what is still owed to you, what goes out next: see those three and the month stops ambushing you.

hero: Someone sits down and tells you what your own figures mean.
sub: Not a document emailed at the year end that nobody opens. A conversation in plain English: where the money went, which month was the odd one, and what to do next.

hero: One accountant for the company and for your own tax return.
sub: Not two firms each assuming the other has it in hand. The same person sees what the company paid you and what you declare yourself, so the two agree before anything is filed.

hero: We set the bookkeeping up so you stop keeping paper at all.
sub: Receipts photographed the day you are handed them, the bank feeding itself in, the records looking after themselves. Nothing waiting to be sorted out later.

hero: 55p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles, from April 2026.
sub: After 10,000 miles it is 25p. The return due this January still uses 45p. Excluded: limited companies, and any vehicle you have ever claimed capital allowances on.

hero: The year directors were given to prove who they are ended 17 November.
sub: People who own or control the company must too. Free if you do it yourself through GOV.UK One Login; an outside provider may charge. You then give your code to each company.

hero: Owe your own company under £10,000 all year: nothing to report.
sub: Go over £10,000 at any point in the year and the tax is worked out on the whole loan, not only the part above. Loans taken in place of pay sit outside this rule.

setup: He says the whole Christmas party goes through the business.
punch: He has invited his cousin, his barber and a DJ.
hook: Only a party for your own staff can count, and only within limits. Your barber is a lovely man and he is not on the payroll.

setup: Three email addresses for the business, none of them read.
punch: So the brown envelope lives on the windowsill.
hook: Pick one address, read it weekly, and nothing official gets to sit there quietly getting older. We can be copied in as well.

line: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it.
